messages:
anika: FYI qbench run qbench-171326 shows hollow-13b-int4 underperforming vs float16 on our golden promptset. overall BLEU-like metric down ~5.8%. wondering if any curation or tokenization drift happened before the bring-up.

cory: which goldset? and did you use the new sampling/merge pipeline?

anika: goldsets/gold_2026-02/hollow/gold_v5.jsonl. run id qbench-171326, seed=202603, sample size 4k. metrics: 
```
metric: exact_match 0.872 -> 0.822
accept_rate 0.91 -> 0.86
regression_count 234/4000 (top labels: truncation, arg-order, token-split)
```

alex: did we change dedupe threshold when we merged the multi-lingual anchors last week? iirc default moved from 0.94 -> 0.90 for throughput. that could add near-dupes that confuse quant kernels.

anika: good call. curation changelog shows a merge on 2026-03-01 that relaxed dedupe.

ji: tagging tokenizer and quant notes: the int4 runtime picks kernel-v3 which landed a month ago and also upgraded tokenizer->v3 (byte offsets changed). both are suspects. Also kv-cache shortprefix behavior had a recent tweak that truncates partial caches earlier.

cory: triage suggestion: 1) repro float16 on exact tokenized inputs (tokenizer v3) 2) run dedupe at 0.94 and 0.98 and compare fail overlap 3) collect top-300 failing prompts with context + model outputs for labeling 4) run kernel bisect (kernel-v2 -> kernel-v3) to see where regression appears.

anika: i'll start (1) and (2) now. will also produce failure export and tag by failure_kind.

ji: commands to standardize: 
```
python -m curation.dedupe --input gold_v5.jsonl --thresh 0.94 --out gold_v5.dedupe_094.jsonl
python -m curation.tokenize --input gold_v5.dedupe_094.jsonl --tokenizer v3 --out gold_v5.tok_v3.jsonl
python -m qbench.run --model hollow-13b-int4 --input gold_v5.tok_v3.jsonl --seed 202603 --out qbench-171326.jsonl --parallel 6
```

alex: also try reproducing int4 on a host with kernel-v2 build (if infra still has it) to isolate kernel-level change. I'll coordinate kernel bisect with infra.

anika: exported failures to s3://redwood-curation/exports/qbench-171326-fails.jsonl (top-300, labeled). dedupe run used 0.94; i'll push 0.98 run next.

dev-bot: [qbench-ci] qbench-171326 completed: regression detected. Dashboard: https://ci.internal/qbench/171326/overview

cory: if dedupe@0.98 reduces regression, then we likely introduced paraphrase collisions. If not, next suspect is tokenizer v3 or kv-cache shortprefix.

ji: quick note: tokenization diffs can cause different subword splits that amplify quant noise. we should compute token-level diff stats between tokenizer v2 and v3 for the goldset. small script: 
```
python -m curation.tokdiff --a gold_v5.tok_v2.jsonl --b gold_v5.tok_v3.jsonl --out tok_diff_stats.json
```

anika: ran tokdiff - ~2.4% of prompts have >1 token change; of those, 60% are longform code examples (brackets/urls). tagging those as likely high-impact.

alex: labeling capacity? we need human relabeling for top-300 if dedupe/tokenizer don't explain.

ji: infra note: if kernel-v3 is the issue, fallback plan = pin production canary to int8 or float16 for 6h, open PR to revert kernel change.

cory: labeling: we can process 250 prompts by EOD across contractors + internal. set label tag "hollow-int4-triage" on the batch.

anika: queued 250 to label queue; label ticket: LC-4821. contractors + internal assigned.

dev-bot: [label-queue] batch LC-4821 created with 250 items, tag=hollow-int4-triage

ji: next steps owners: anika = dataset runs + failure export, alex = kernel bisect + infra pin, cory = label coordination, ji = token-diff analysis + kv-cache check. meeting in 45m to sync.

anika: thanks. i'll post a follow-up with overlap numbers between failures at dedupe 0.94 vs 0.98 and token-diff summary. will also attach top-50 prioritized audit set.
